newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 15.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on April 15. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto has said despite rapid development in the country, social and economic disparities still exist. Suharto said the government was determined to eradicate poverty in Indonesia, a multi-ethnic country with 200 million people.

Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana, who originally said that Sunday's 10-hour blackout was because of technical trouble, said that the state-owned electricity company PLN deliberately cut power so it could do repair work.

The prosecution in the subversion trial of chairman of the left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD) Budiman Sudjatmiko has asked the central Jakarta district court to sentence him to 15 years in jail for undermining the state ideology Pancasila.

The Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) has denied its members were involved in the recent political riots in Wonosobo and Banjarnegara in Central Java. The party said the riots were masterminded by hoodlums and former convicts.
